head_commit.message:
KAFKA-20901: Enforce cordoned log directories configured with relative paths (#23241)

Kafka allows `log.dirs `to be configured with relative paths, but
`cordoned.log.dirs` was validated and applied using the original
configuration strings, whereas `LogManager` converts log directories to
absolute paths and uses those paths for directory ID lookups.

As a result, configuring `cordoned.log.dirs` with the absolute path
reported by `DescribeLogDirs` was rejected when `log.dirs` contained the
equivalent relative path. Using the relative path passed validation, but
it did not match the absolute path used internally, so the directory was
not reported as cordoned to the controller.

This change consistently uses absolute paths when validating and
applying `cordoned.log.dirs`, including during dynamic reconfiguration
and broker heartbeat propagation.

Reviewers: Mickael Maison <mickael.maison@gmail.com>

head_commit.message:
MINOR: Derive SSL principal from the matched groups in SslPrincipalMapper (#24010)

SslPrincipalMapper.Rule.apply checks the rule with Matcher.matches() but
then builds the principal with String.replaceAll, which scans the DN
again and can use a different match. For some rules (unanchored, or with
alternation) this gives a wrong name, e.g. "bobeng" instead of "bob", or
the replacement applied twice.

Build the name from the same match with Matcher.appendReplacement. A
rule that produces an empty name is now treated as not matching, so the
next rule applies, the same way an invalid result is handled for
Kerberos rules.

Added unit tests in SslPrincipalMapperTest.

Reviewers: Manikumar Reddy <manikumar@confluent.io>

display_title: MINOR: validate partition in DefaultForeignResponseSinkPartitioner

head_commit.message:
MINOR: validate partition in DefaultForeignResponseSinkPartitioner

DefaultForeignResponseSinkPartitioner routes foreign-key join responses to the
partition stored in the subscription record, without checking it against the
number of partitions. A negative value makes the ProducerRecord constructor
throw and fails the task, and a value that is too large fails the send.

Fall back to the default partitioner, as for subscriptions without a
partition, when the partition is outside [0, numPartitions), and log a warning.

Added unit tests in KTableImplTest and KTableKTableForeignKeyJoinScenarioTest.

head_commit.message:
MINOR: Derive SSL principal from the matched groups in SslPrincipalMapper (#24010)

SslPrincipalMapper.Rule.apply checks the rule with Matcher.matches() but
then builds the principal with String.replaceAll, which scans the DN
again and can use a different match. For some rules (unanchored, or with
alternation) this gives a wrong name, e.g. "bobeng" instead of "bob", or
the replacement applied twice.

Build the name from the same match with Matcher.appendReplacement. A
rule that produces an empty name is now treated as not matching, so the
next rule applies, the same way an invalid result is handled for
Kerberos rules.

Added unit tests in SslPrincipalMapperTest.

Reviewers: Manikumar Reddy <manikumar@confluent.io>

warm-up. The metadata shows it only until the promotion, so a test
thread stalled for about two heartbeat intervals missed it and timed
out. Record the warm-up's start and its promotion through a
StandbyUpdateListener instead.

name: Pull Request
display_title: MINOR: derive SSL principal from the matched groups in SslPrincipalMapper

head_commit.message:
MINOR: derive SSL principal from the matched groups in SslPrincipalMapper

SslPrincipalMapper.Rule.apply checks the rule with Matcher.matches() but then
builds the principal with String.replaceAll, which scans the DN again and can
use a different match. For some rules (unanchored, or with alternation) this
gives a wrong name, e.g. "bobeng" instead of "bob", or the replacement
applied twice.

Build the name from the same match with Matcher.appendReplacement. A rule that
produces an empty name is now treated as not matching, so the next rule
applies, the same way an invalid result is handled for Kerberos rules.

Added unit tests in SslPrincipalMapperTest.

name: Pull Request Labeled
display_title: MINOR: improve SubscriptionWrapperSerde

head_commit.message:
MINOR: improve SubscriptionWrapperSerde

SubscriptionWrapperSerde.deserialize computes the primary key length from the
record size without checking that the record is long enough, so a truncated
record fails with NegativeArraySizeException or BufferUnderflowException.

Check the record length against the fixed header (2 bytes, optional 16-byte
hash, 4-byte partition for version 1) before reading, and reject unknown
versions before parsing, so these cases fail with a clear
SerializationException / UnsupportedVersionException instead.

name: Pull Request Reviewed
display_title: KAFKA-21111 [3/N]: Promote the standby of an orphan on a member that cannot report its progress

head_commit.message:
Promote an unobservable standby only when the target owner's process holds no copy

A copy on the target owner's process is warmer than one of unknown lag elsewhere, and is what a hand-over that is already under way completes with. Right after a coordinator failover, no copy reports its lag, so without this the refiner would undo such hand-overs in favour of a standby on another process. When the target owner has left the group, an orphan now also runs on such a standby holder until the next assignor run.

name: Pull Request Labeled
display_title: KAFKA-21111 [3/N]: Promote the standby of an orphan on a member that cannot report its progress

head_commit.message:
Promote an unobservable standby only when the target owner's process holds no copy

A copy on the target owner's process is warmer than one of unknown lag elsewhere, and is what a hand-over that is already under way completes with. Right after a coordinator failover, no copy reports its lag, so without this the refiner would undo such hand-overs in favour of a standby on another process. When the target owner has left the group, an orphan now also runs on such a standby holder until the next assignor run.

name: Pull Request Reviewed
display_title: KAFKA-21389: Keep a ready streams member ready on ASSIGNMENT_DELAYED

head_commit.message:
MINOR: Keep a ready streams member ready on ASSIGNMENT_DELAYED

The group coordinator returns ASSIGNMENT_DELAYED both during the initial
rebalance delay of a new group and when it defers computing a new target
assignment because of the configured assignment interval. In the second
case the member keeps its current assignment, but the client mapped the
status to isGroupReady=false, which made the StreamThread stop processing
all owned tasks until a later heartbeat no longer carried the status.

ASSIGNMENT_DELAYED now keeps the readiness of the previous target
assignment. A member that has not been ready yet, including one waiting
out the initial rebalance delay, stays not ready, while a ready member
keeps processing. Missing or incorrectly partitioned topics still mark
the group as not ready, also when reported together with
ASSIGNMENT_DELAYED.

head_commit.message:
KAFKA-21214: Start the new map of a member at the default capacity (follow-up) (#24001)

A member that owns no partitions gets its new map from
`Utils.newHashMap(0)` in `AssignmentBuilder.ownedPartitions`. Its table
starts with a single slot and resizes at 1, 2, 4 and 7 entries before
reaching the default capacity of 16. This patch sizes the map for at
least 12 entries, which a map of the default capacity holds without
resizing.

head_commit.message:
KAFKA-20866: Remove incremental-only append result state (#23749)

RecordAppendResult is created for every successful append. This change
removes the incremental-strategy-only outcome and extensionBytesNeeded
fields from regular results. Buffer-extension capacity is now held only
by a private result subtype, while the existing append/new-batch
behavior remains unchanged.

The chunked accumulator consumes the capacity through a package-private
accessor, and a regression test covers the buffer-extension result
contract.

name: Pull Request Reviewed
display_title: KAFKA-21389: Keep a ready streams member ready on ASSIGNMENT_DELAYED

head_commit.message:
MINOR: Keep a ready streams member ready on ASSIGNMENT_DELAYED

The group coordinator returns ASSIGNMENT_DELAYED both during the initial
rebalance delay of a new group and when it defers computing a new target
assignment because of the configured assignment interval. In the second
case the member keeps its current assignment, but the client mapped the
status to isGroupReady=false, which made the StreamThread stop processing
all owned tasks until a later heartbeat no longer carried the status.

ASSIGNMENT_DELAYED now keeps the readiness of the previous target
assignment. A member that has not been ready yet, including one waiting
out the initial rebalance delay, stays not ready, while a ready member
keeps processing. Missing or incorrectly partitioned topics still mark
the group as not ready, also when reported together with
ASSIGNMENT_DELAYED.

head_commit.message:
KAFKA-16304: Report file read errors from SslTransportLayer.transferFrom as such (#23928)

Follow-up to #23445, under the same ticket (resolved, fix version
4.5.0).

Since #23445, a failed send of fetched records is passed to a handler
that re-reads the region on the scheduler, and the log directory is
offlined only if the re-read fails too. The re-read is needed because
over PLAINTEXT `sendfile` reads the file and writes the socket in one
call, so a disk error and a socket error are the same bare
`IOException`. `SslTransportLayer.transferFrom` does not have that
problem: it reads the file with `FileChannel.read`, then encrypts and
writes, so it knows which of the two failed. As discussed on #23445,
this passes that on instead of finding it out again:

* `SslTransportLayer.transferFrom` throws a new `FileReadException`, an
  `IOException` with the position of the read, when `FileChannel.read`
  or `FileChannel.size` fails. A `ClosedChannelException`, from a
  deletion or a shutdown, is rethrown as is
  (`FileReadException.ofReadFailure`).
* `TransferableChannel.distinguishesFileReadFailures()` says whether a
  transport does that: true for TLS, false, the default, for
  PLAINTEXT.
* `FileRecords.writeTo` passes to the handler a `FileReadException`
  always, a `ClosedChannelException` never, and any other
  `IOException` only if the transport cannot tell a failed read of the
  file from a failed write to the network channel. A failure of its own
  `channel.size()` call before the transfer becomes a
  `FileReadException` as well, unless it is a `ClosedChannelException`.
* `LocalLog` reports a `FileReadException` as a failure of the log
  directory right away, without re-reading the region. Other failures
  are re-read on the scheduler as before.
* `LogDirFailureChannel.maybeAddOfflineLogDir` logs the error only when
  it takes the log directory offline, so that the failures that follow
  in a failing directory do not flood the log.

Consequences worth stating:

* On TLS listeners a disconnect no longer re-reads the region that was
  being sent. In the test notes, consumers killed mid-fetch over TLS
  for 5 minutes made the scheduler re-read 151 MB without this change
  and nothing with it.
* On TLS listeners a read error now offlines the log directory even if
  the region could be read again by the time of a re-read, e.g. after a
  transient media error. Before, such an error was attributed to the
  socket. This is the criterion `LocalLog` applies to any other
  `IOException`.
* A failed `FileChannel.size()` call on the segment, over either
  transport, is now reported as a read failure without a re-read.
* For every caller of `maybeAddOfflineLogDir`, an error in a log
  directory that is already offline is no longer logged there.
* PLAINTEXT listeners still re-read: `sendfile` cannot tell the two
  apart.
* KRaft snapshots, sent through `UnalignedFileRecords`, are still not
  covered.

A member that owns no partitions gets its new map from
`Utils.newHashMap(0)` in `AssignmentBuilder.ownedPartitions`. Its table
starts with a single slot and resizes at 1, 2, 4 and 7 entries before
reaching the default capacity of 16. This patch sizes the map for at
least 12 entries, which a map of the default capacity holds without
resizing.

display_title: MINOR: Avoid per-record leader epoch `Optional` allocation in `CompletedFetch` and `ShareCompletedFetch`

head_commit.message:
MINOR: Avoid allocating the leader epoch Optional per record in CompletedFetch and ShareCompletedFetch

CompletedFetch#fetchRecords and ShareCompletedFetch#fetchRecords called
maybeLeaderEpoch(currentBatch.partitionLeaderEpoch()) for every returned
record, allocating a new Optional (and a boxed Integer for epochs > 127)
per record, although the value only changes per batch. CompletedFetch
already computes exactly this value once per batch into lastEpoch.

Reuse the per-batch Optional instead: CompletedFetch passes lastEpoch,
ShareCompletedFetch computes it once when it advances to the next batch.
Optional is immutable, so sharing one instance between the records of a
batch does not change observable behaviour.

CompletedFetchBenchmark (500 records, 5 batches) shows 16 B/record less
allocation for small epochs and 32 B/record for epochs > 127.

KAFKA-16304: Report file read errors from SslTransportLayer.transferFrom as such (#23928)

Follow-up to #23445, under the same ticket (resolved, fix version
4.5.0).

Since #23445, a failed send of fetched records is passed to a handler
that re-reads the region on the scheduler, and the log directory is
offlined only if the re-read fails too. The re-read is needed because
over PLAINTEXT `sendfile` reads the file and writes the socket in one
call, so a disk error and a socket error are the same bare
`IOException`. `SslTransportLayer.transferFrom` does not have that
problem: it reads the file with `FileChannel.read`, then encrypts and
writes, so it knows which of the two failed. As discussed on #23445,
this passes that on instead of finding it out again:

* `SslTransportLayer.transferFrom` throws a new `FileReadException`, an
  `IOException` with the position of the read, when `FileChannel.read`
  or `FileChannel.size` fails. A `ClosedChannelException`, from a
  deletion or a shutdown, is rethrown as is
  (`FileReadException.ofReadFailure`).
* `TransferableChannel.distinguishesFileReadFailures()` says whether a
  transport does that: true for TLS, false, the default, for
  PLAINTEXT.
* `FileRecords.writeTo` passes to the handler a `FileReadException`
  always, a `ClosedChannelException` never, and any other
  `IOException` only if the transport cannot tell a failed read of the
  file from a failed write to the network channel. A failure of its own
  `channel.size()` call before the transfer becomes a
  `FileReadException` as well, unless it is a `ClosedChannelException`.
* `LocalLog` reports a `FileReadException` as a failure of the log
  directory right away, without re-reading the region. Other failures
  are re-read on the scheduler as before.
* `LogDirFailureChannel.maybeAddOfflineLogDir` logs the error only when
  it takes the log directory offline, so that the failures that follow
  in a failing directory do not flood the log.

Consequences worth stating:

* On TLS listeners a disconnect no longer re-reads the region that was
  being sent. In the test notes, consumers killed mid-fetch over TLS
  for 5 minutes made the scheduler re-read 151 MB without this change
  and nothing with it.
* On TLS listeners a read error now offlines the log directory even if
  the region could be read again by the time of a re-read, e.g. after a
  transient media error. Before, such an error was attributed to the
  socket. This is the criterion `LocalLog` applies to any other
  `IOException`.
* A failed `FileChannel.size()` call on the segment, over either
  transport, is now reported as a read failure without a re-read.
* For every caller of `maybeAddOfflineLogDir`, an error in a log
  directory that is already offline is no longer logged there.
* PLAINTEXT listeners still re-read: `sendfile` cannot tell the two
  apart.
* KRaft snapshots, sent through `UnalignedFileRecords`, are still not
  covered.

head_commit.message:
KAFKA-21214: Start the new map of a member at the default capacity (follow-up)

A member that owns no partitions gets its new map from
`Utils.newHashMap(0)` in `AssignmentBuilder.ownedPartitions`. Its table
starts with a single slot and resizes at 1, 2, 4 and 7 entries before
reaching the default capacity of 16. This patch sizes the map for at
least 12 entries, which a map of the default capacity holds without
resizing.

head_commit.message:
KAFKA-21214: Start the new map of a member at the default capacity (follow-up)

A member that owns no partitions gets its new map from
`Utils.newHashMap(0)` in `AssignmentBuilder.ownedPartitions`. Its table
starts with a single slot and resizes at 1, 2, 4 and 7 entries before
reaching the default capacity of 16. This patch sizes the map for at
least 12 entries, which a map of the default capacity holds without
resizing.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

No test covered how TaskManager#setProcessingThreadsPaused forwards

mocks TaskManager.

head_commit.message:
KAFKA-16304: Report file read errors from SslTransportLayer.transferFrom as such (#23928)

Follow-up to #23445, under the same ticket (resolved, fix version
4.5.0).

Since #23445, a failed send of fetched records is passed to a handler
that re-reads the region on the scheduler, and the log directory is
offlined only if the re-read fails too. The re-read is needed because
over PLAINTEXT `sendfile` reads the file and writes the socket in one
call, so a disk error and a socket error are the same bare
`IOException`. `SslTransportLayer.transferFrom` does not have that
problem: it reads the file with `FileChannel.read`, then encrypts and
writes, so it knows which of the two failed. As discussed on #23445,
this passes that on instead of finding it out again:

* `SslTransportLayer.transferFrom` throws a new `FileReadException`, an
  `IOException` with the position of the read, when `FileChannel.read`
  or `FileChannel.size` fails. A `ClosedChannelException`, from a
  deletion or a shutdown, is rethrown as is
  (`FileReadException.ofReadFailure`).
* `TransferableChannel.distinguishesFileReadFailures()` says whether a
  transport does that: true for TLS, false, the default, for
  PLAINTEXT.
* `FileRecords.writeTo` passes to the handler a `FileReadException`
  always, a `ClosedChannelException` never, and any other
  `IOException` only if the transport cannot tell a failed read of the
  file from a failed write to the network channel. A failure of its own
  `channel.size()` call before the transfer becomes a
  `FileReadException` as well, unless it is a `ClosedChannelException`.
* `LocalLog` reports a `FileReadException` as a failure of the log
  directory right away, without re-reading the region. Other failures
  are re-read on the scheduler as before.
* `LogDirFailureChannel.maybeAddOfflineLogDir` logs the error only when
  it takes the log directory offline, so that the failures that follow
  in a failing directory do not flood the log.

Consequences worth stating:

* On TLS listeners a disconnect no longer re-reads the region that was
  being sent. In the test notes, consumers killed mid-fetch over TLS
  for 5 minutes made the scheduler re-read 151 MB without this change
  and nothing with it.
* On TLS listeners a read error now offlines the log directory even if
  the region could be read again by the time of a re-read, e.g. after a
  transient media error. Before, such an error was attributed to the
  socket. This is the criterion `LocalLog` applies to any other
  `IOException`.
* A failed `FileChannel.size()` call on the segment, over either
  transport, is now reported as a read failure without a re-read.
* For every caller of `maybeAddOfflineLogDir`, an error in a log
  directory that is already offline is no longer logged there.
* PLAINTEXT listeners still re-read: `sendfile` cannot tell the two
  apart.
* KRaft snapshots, sent through `UnalignedFileRecords`, are still not
  covered.

head_commit.message:
KAFKA-21214: [8/8] Add the uniform2 consumer group assignor (#23723)

The uniform assignor balances the total number of partitions per member
but not the partitions of each topic: with homogeneous subscriptions, a
member can get all the partitions of a topic while the others get none
of them. The throughput is usually about the same across the partitions
of a topic but not across topics, so adding members does not spread the
load.

This patch adds uniform2, the next version of the uniform assignor, from
the steps of the previous patches. It lives next to the uniform assignor
while it is developed and is not registered as a built-in assignor. Its
assignments have these properties, in priority order:
- Every partition of every subscribed topic goes to exactly one of its
  subscribers.
- Every subscriber of a topic gets the same number of its partitions,
  the minimum quota, or one more, with an extra partition.
- No extra partition could move to another subscriber of its topic
  whose assignment is at least two partitions smaller.
- Partitions stay with their owners where the above allows. The
  placement moves the fewest partitions for the quotas, and an
  assignment that already has these properties is returned unchanged.
- The result is deterministic.

Changes:
- `Uniform2Assignor` and `AssignmentBuilder`, which reads the group,
  runs the `KeepStickyExtraPartitions`, `AssignRemainingExtraPartitions`
  and `BalanceExtraPartitions` steps on the quotas, places every topic
  and builds the result. Partitions of topics that a member does not
  subscribe to or which no longer exist are dropped. The class Javadoc
  of `Uniform2Assignor` describes the steps with a worked example.
- The result reuses the maps and sets of the members that do not change.
  `RangeSet` becomes public to return consecutive partitions.
- The assignor does not use racks yet. Rack awareness comes in a later
  patch.
- `ConsumerAssignorBenchmark` gets `UNIFORM2`.
- End to end tests with hand traced expectations, written with the group
  spec and topics fixtures, and a shared checker of the properties.

Reviewers: Sean Quah <squah@confluent.io>

---------

head_commit.message:
KAFKA-21230: Bound commit memory in the uncommitted-bytes limit

A thread pauses processing and commits when its uncommitted bytes pass
its share of statestore.uncommitted.max.bytes. A commit can itself need
extra memory. The thread can therefore go over the limit while it
commits.

Stores commit one at a time. During the commit of one store, the extra
memory needed is up to the size of that store's uncommitted data. The
largest store gives the worst case.

Add maxStoreUncommittedBytes to ProcessorStateManager, Task and
TaskManager. It returns the largest uncommitted byte count of any one
store. StreamThread now adds this value to the total uncommitted bytes
before it compares the sum with the limit.

Apply the same check to the global state thread. Add
maxStoreUncommittedBytes to GlobalStateManager and
GlobalStateMaintainer, and make GlobalStreamThread compare the total
plus the largest store's bytes with its limit.

Both threads now commit earlier, so the commit stays inside the limit.
Update the statestore.uncommitted.max.bytes documentation and the 4.5.0
upgrade guide to describe the new check and how it changes the point of
an early commit compared with 4.4.

but not the partitions of each topic: with homogeneous subscriptions, a
member can get all the partitions of a topic while the others get none
of them. The throughput is usually about the same across the partitions
of a topic but not across topics, so adding members does not spread the
load.

the steps of the previous patches. It lives next to the uniform assignor
while it is developed and is not registered as a built-in assignor. Its
assignments have these properties, in priority order:
- Every partition of every subscribed topic goes to exactly one of its
  subscribers.
- Every subscriber of a topic gets the same number of its partitions,
  the minimum quota, or one more, with an extra partition.
- No extra partition could move to another subscriber of its topic
  whose assignment is at least two partitions smaller.

  placement moves the fewest partitions for the quotas, and an
  assignment that already has these properties is returned unchanged.

name: Pull Request Reviewed
display_title: KAFKA-21230: Pause task executors on byte limit

head_commit.message:
KAFKA-21230: Pause processing threads when group not ready

When processing threads are enabled and the Streams group becomes not
ready, runOnceWithProcessingThreads returns early. Thus it does not
call maybePauseProcessingForUncommittedBytes(). But the thread keeps
its tasks, and the task executors continue to process them. Nothing
commits, so the uncommitted bytes can increase without a limit.

runOnceWithProcessingThreads now calls
maybePauseProcessingForUncommittedBytes() before the early return. The
byte limit then applies while the group is not ready.

A new StreamThreadTest test,
shouldPauseProcessingThreadsWhileUncommittedBytesExceedLimitAndStreamsGroupNotReady,
covers the change from a ready group to a group that is not ready.

name: Pull Request Reviewed
display_title: KAFKA-21355: Add a fuzzer for the uniform2 assignor

head_commit.message:
KAFKA-21355: Add a fuzzer for the uniform2 assignor

The unit tests of the uniform2 assignor check hand traced cases, but its
properties must hold for any group and any sequence of changes.

This patch adds a fuzzer checking them on random groups and random
sequences of events: members joining and leaving, one at a time or
several, topics gaining partitions, and subscriptions changing. Other
events make the input stale, as the coordinator can pass it to the
assignor, such as topics deleted or created again while members still
hold their partitions, and empty subscriptions.

Changes:
- `Uniform2FuzzScenario` generates the groups and the events, and passes
  every group to the assignor as a group spec built with
  `GroupSpecFixture`.
- `Uniform2AssignorFuzzTest` checks validity, spread and balance,
  determinism under shuffled inputs, the fixed point with the same map
  instances, the same map for every member whose partitions do not
  change, the movement bounds after a single leave or join, and the
  moves of tiny groups, at most one above the fewest found by a brute
  force oracle.
- It also checks that the two ways of counting of the balance step give
  the same quotas, and that a run of at least 2,000 events goes through
  every kind of event.
- The default run takes seconds, and environment variables scale it up,
  see the class Javadoc.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

display_title: KAFKA-21214: [8/8] Add the uniform2 consumer group assignor (#23723)

head_commit.message:
KAFKA-21214: [8/8] Add the uniform2 consumer group assignor (#23723)

The uniform assignor balances the total number of partitions per member
but not the partitions of each topic: with homogeneous subscriptions, a
member can get all the partitions of a topic while the others get none
of them. The throughput is usually about the same across the partitions
of a topic but not across topics, so adding members does not spread the
load.

This patch adds uniform2, the next version of the uniform assignor, from
the steps of the previous patches. It lives next to the uniform assignor
while it is developed and is not registered as a built-in assignor. Its
assignments have these properties, in priority order:
- Every partition of every subscribed topic goes to exactly one of its
  subscribers.
- Every subscriber of a topic gets the same number of its partitions,
  the minimum quota, or one more, with an extra partition.
- No extra partition could move to another subscriber of its topic
  whose assignment is at least two partitions smaller.
- Partitions stay with their owners where the above allows. The
  placement moves the fewest partitions for the quotas, and an
  assignment that already has these properties is returned unchanged.
- The result is deterministic.

Changes:
- `Uniform2Assignor` and `AssignmentBuilder`, which reads the group,
  runs the `KeepStickyExtraPartitions`, `AssignRemainingExtraPartitions`
  and `BalanceExtraPartitions` steps on the quotas, places every topic
  and builds the result. Partitions of topics that a member does not
  subscribe to or which no longer exist are dropped. The class Javadoc
  of `Uniform2Assignor` describes the steps with a worked example.
- The result reuses the maps and sets of the members that do not change.
  `RangeSet` becomes public to return consecutive partitions.
- The assignor does not use racks yet. Rack awareness comes in a later
  patch.
- `ConsumerAssignorBenchmark` gets `UNIFORM2`.
- End to end tests with hand traced expectations, written with the group
  spec and topics fixtures, and a shared checker of the properties.

Reviewers: Sean Quah <squah@confluent.io>

head_commit.message:
KAFKA-21356: Relieve the persister thread of share group DLQ processing. (#23964)

Copying records into the DLQ was dominated by work on the persister
thread, which also completes write responses for every share partition:

- isDlqEnabledOnTopic and dlqTopicMaxMessageBytes built a LogConfig,
which parses every topic config, on each DLQ request. Read the one key
directly. (Affects both copy on and off case)
- The source record read of ran synchronously on the persister thread.
Run it (and later rounds) on a single-threaded fetch executor owned and
shut down by BrokerServer. (Affects copy on case)
- ShareGroupDLQRecordFetcher.collectRecords visited every batch of a 1
MiB log read, loading each file-backed batch from disk, although a
request wants a few records. We can simply reject batches where the
batch baseOffset > dlq endoffset (V2 only, Affects copy on case).
Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
